brief.topic: Latency vs quality: when a faster, smaller model is the better product
brief.audience: PMs choosing models for user-facing AI features
constraints: Illustrative numbers labelled on screen and in caption

coreInsight: Speed is part of quality: route narrow, easy requests to a smaller, faster model when your eval shows no meaningful drop, and keep the large model as the fallback for hard cases.

hooks.text: The best model can make a worse product.
hooks.notes: Good tension, less specific about why.

hooks.notes: Clear but reads as a lecture.

caption.opening: A slightly better answer that arrives much later can be the worse product.
body:
A smaller, faster model is often the right call when:
→ the task is narrow: classify, extract, rewrite, route
→ your eval set shows no meaningful quality drop
→ a person is waiting on the answer
→ a larger model is still there for the hard cases
Route by difficulty, measure both speed and quality, and decide with your own eval set rather than a public leaderboard.
(The 8 s vs 2 s in the reel is an illustrative example, not a benchmark.)

claims.text: For narrow, user-facing tasks, a smaller and faster model with a large-model fallback is often the better product, if evaluation shows no meaningful quality loss.
8 seconds per answer with a large model on every request vs 2 seconds with easy requests routed to a small model.
